questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Although Harappa was the first site to be discovered, it was badly destroyed by brick-robbers. As early as 1875, Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology, noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay brick for 'about 100 miles' of the railway line between Lahore and Multan. Many of the ancient structures at the site were damaged. In contrast, Mohenjodaro was far better preserved. Cunningham, when excavating, found an ancient seal that was given to him. He tried to place it within the time-frame of the sixth century BCE to fourth century CE, the period of the earliest cities he was familiar with from Chinese pilgrim accounts, and thus missed the true antiquity of the Indus Valley."

What critical chronological error did Alexander Cunningham make when attempting to date Harappan artefacts?

options.text: He dated them to the European Middle Ages
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: He tried to fit Harappan seals within the time-frame of early historic cities (6th c. BCE to 4th c. CE) known from Chinese pilgrim chronicles
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for The Plight of Harappa.

options.text: He believed they were manufactured in 18th-century Bengal
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: He considered them to be modern forgeries made by railway workers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology (Bricks, Beads and Bones) (The Plight of Harappa):
He tried to fit Harappan seals within the time-frame of early historic cities (6th c. BCE to 4th c. CE) known from Chinese pilgrim chronicles

Detailed Analysis:
1. Cunningham relied on records of Chinese Buddhist pilgrims (Faxian and Xuanzang) and assumed Indian urbanization began in the 6th century BCE, missing Harappa's 3rd millennium BCE antiquity.
Hence, Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Saddle querns are found in considerable numbers at Harappan sites, and they seem to have been the only means in use for grinding cereals. As a rule, they were roughly made of hard, gritty, igneous rock or sandstone and mostly show signs of hard usage. As their bases are usually convex, they must have been set in the earth or in mud to prevent their rocking. Two main types have been found: those on which another smaller stone was pushed or rolled to and fro, and others with which a second stone was used as a pounder, eventually making a large cavity in the nether stone. Querns of the former type were probably used solely for grain; the second type were possibly used only for pounding herbs and spices for making curries. In fact, stones of this latter type are dubbed 'curry stones' by our workmen and our cook asked for the loan of one from the museum for use in the kitchen."

questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Although Harappa was the first site to be discovered, it was badly destroyed by brick-robbers. As early as 1875, Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology, noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay brick for 'about 100 miles' of the railway line between Lahore and Multan. Many of the ancient structures at the site were damaged. In contrast, Mohenjodaro was far better preserved. Cunningham, when excavating, found an ancient seal that was given to him. He tried to place it within the time-frame of the sixth century BCE to fourth century CE, the period of the earliest cities he was familiar with from Chinese pilgrim accounts, and thus missed the true antiquity of the Indus Valley."

What critical chronological error did Alexander Cunningham make when attempting to date Harappan artefacts?

options.text: He tried to fit Harappan seals within the time-frame of early historic cities (6th c. BCE to 4th c. CE) known from Chinese pilgrim chronicles
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: He dated them to the European Middle Ages
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: He believed they were manufactured in 18th-century Bengal
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: He considered them to be modern forgeries made by railway workers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Cunningham relied on records of Chinese Buddhist pilgrims (Faxian and Xuanzang) and assumed Indian urbanization began in the 6th century BCE, missing Harappa's 3rd millennium BCE antiquity.
Hence, Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.
